recognize_zh: 抹片體部可見一團無結構、淡藍紫色的均質沉積物（箭頭），內外夾雜被困住的紅血球，周邊白血球形態正常；這種淡藍色無細胞團塊是冷凝球蛋白（cryoglobulin）在室溫下沉澱的表現。
features: Irregular, amorphous, homogeneous pale blue-violet extracellular deposit in the body of the smear (arrow)
Red cells trapped at the edges of and overlying the deposit, some distorted
Deposit is acellular without internal structure, nuclei or granules
Background red cells normochromic with mild anisocytosis; neutrophils morphologically unremarkable
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows an irregular, acellular, pale blue amorphous extracellular deposit in the body of the smear, with red cells trapped at its margins. The surrounding red cells are normochromic with mild anisocytosis, and the neutrophils appear morphologically unremarkable. In a patient with lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma, these pale blue precipitates are suggestive of cryoglobulin deposition; confirmation requires a warm-collected sample for cryoglobulin testing, and repeat smears from a prewarmed specimen should lack the deposits.

ddx.vs: Smudged cells retain nuclear chromatin strands and are purple, whereas cryoglobulin deposits are nuclei-free pale blue homogeneous material.
High paraprotein produces diffuse bluish background staining and rouleaux throughout the smear rather than discrete globular clumps.
Stain precipitate is dark, granular and crystalline, not pale homogeneous amorphous material.
Platelet clumps are granular aggregates of individual platelets with purple granulomere, unlike structureless pale blue deposits.
